why: Check 1 holds to its expect line. It passes when loadConfig from src/config.js returns {} on malformed JSON without throwing. Its FAIL cases are throwing, a non-zero exit, a result other than {}, or loadConfig not exported, and a call can't be made without the export. It says stderr output "does not matter", and the stricter checks (valid JSON still parses, a missing file still throws, the warning, README) are under Advisory. Check 2 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition requires "the node --test summary reports 0 failed tests and at least 1 passing test." The words "npm test passes" only require the test run to succeed (exit 0). They don't require a minimum number of passing tests, so this extra condition belongs under Advisory, not in PASS. It also conflicts with the FAIL condition, which doesn't treat a run with zero tests as a failure.
